A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPathAgent work. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original patch-level VQA, huge-region analysis, WSI classification, description-generation comparisons, and pathologist evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds external-cohort evaluations, PathMMU-Pro results, and component ablations.

M1.justification: The Qwen3-14B/CPath-CLIP architecture, three-stage training, and screening–navigation–reasoning pipeline are retained. The expanded workflow description documents operations already represented in v1's examples and prompts; the corresponding training and inference prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained PathMMU and TCGA evaluations, v2 adds CPTAC-Lung WSI classification and BRACS benign/atypical/malignant region classification, extending evaluation to external cohorts. PathMMU-Pro adds questions designed to require visual discrimination while reducing textual shortcuts (Section 4.4 and Appendix B.3).

E2.justification: v2 adds CPath-Omni to the PathMMU-HR² comparison and a retrained CPath-Omni* to TCGA WSI classification. PRISM and TITAN become evaluated comparators in Figure 4. Quilt-LLaVA and PathGen-LLaVA WSI comparisons already existed in v1's Table 4 and are relocated into Table 3.

E3.justification: New controls replace learned screening with random selection of 70% of regions and replace navigation/reasoning with single-view descriptions. The added CPath-Omni* comparison uses matched-split retraining. PathMMU-HR²'s reported total changes from 1,688 to 1,668, matching the unchanged tissue counts; this supports a reporting correction, not an inference that the benchmark was resampled.

E4.justification: v2 adds component ablations, external-distribution testing, and a shortcut-focused PathMMU-Pro analysis, addressing component contributions, generalization, and benchmark bias. The 40-region pathologist study and Gemini agent failure analysis are retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report MIL results averaged over five random seeds and pass@k from eight generations across 40 regions. Relocating and explaining the pathologist study adds no new repetition or uncertainty-reporting practice. No confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: New results include 88.1% CPTAC-Lung and 64.3% BRACS balanced accuracy, 65.3% PathMMU-Pro full-set accuracy, and 80.3%/75.0% WSI balanced accuracy for the two component ablations. New comparisons place TITAN ahead on CPTAC-Lung and experts ahead on PathMMU-Pro Tiny. Existing CPathAgent headline scores in Tables 1–3 are retained; these additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds set and tuple notation for region grouping, prioritization, and navigation paths already documented through v1's examples and prompts. This is a formal restatement of the workflow, without new mathematical properties, substantive assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contribution lists, and conclusions retain the same central claims: a pathologist-like agent, unified multiscale training, an expert-validated huge-region benchmark, and strong performance across three image scales. Rewriting and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the above-expert PathMMU results through discussion of textual shortcuts and the expert lead on PathMMU-Pro. It adds interpretations of component contributions and OOD performance. Appendix D introduces substantive limitations concerning synthetic rather than observed clinical trajectories, restricted task scope, and training-data scale.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents patient-level splitting, clarifies that the complete cropped-view sequence enters reasoning together, and describes matched-split CPath-Omni retraining. Appendix C.2 adds benchmark construction details. Hardware, stage runtimes, optimization hyperparameters, and detailed prompts remain unchanged, with no new code or data access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting CPTAC-Lung, BRACS, and PathMMU-Pro, and extends positioning against PRISM and TITAN through generalization and data-efficiency comparisons. The established distinction from static pathology models and PathFinder remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and methods receive extensive rewriting. Workflow explanations expand while the training description is condensed. The pathologist evaluation moves into Appendix B.2, WSI comparisons are consolidated, and the appendices are reorganized around a new limitations section.

P2.justification: v1's architecture/training Figure 4 is removed, a new OOD Figure 4 is added, and the pass@k plot moves and is redrawn as Figure A9. WSI tables are consolidated and reorganized, while Tables A4–A5 introduce benchmark and ablation displays. The remaining appendix examples and prompts are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: External-cohort tests and direct component ablations address important gaps in v1's evidence for generalization and component effectiveness. PathMMU-Pro evaluation and explicit limitations also improve the calibration of claims about expert-level reasoning and clinical applicability. These are substantial gains in validation, although the new data-efficiency comparison needs qualification: its 5,254-WSI count excludes the larger screening-overview pool documented in Appendix A.1.
